limitations.text: COVID-OUT enrolled adults with overweight or obesity and no known prior infection; ACTIV-6 allowed prior infection and vaccination.
The COVID-OUT report has an indexed correction and conflicting cumulative-incidence values, making its absolute risk reduction uncertain.

synthesisRows.title: Vorinostat computational nomination for anti-TNF-refractory Crohn disease
synthesisRows.use: Computational drug-repurposing hypothesis for anti-TNF-refractory Crohn disease
synthesisRows.population: GSE100833 anti-TNF refractory Crohn's disease inflamed and non-inflamed colonic transcriptomes; CMap and STRING analyses.

synthesisRows.endpoint: Connectivity Map (CMap) enrichment score for a selected gene cluster
synthesisRows.timepoint: Computational analysis; no patient treatment follow-up

finding.text: Vorinostat was nominated by an original computational analysis of Crohn disease transcriptomes. The result identifies a hypothesis for experimental testing and does not demonstrate symptom improvement, remission or clinical safety.

synthesisRows.magnitudeText: CMap enrichment score 12.3, cluster 1. This is a computational score, not a clinical effect size; a clinical effect interval is not identifiable from this design.
synthesisRows.evidenceBase: One original computational analysis; the source describes transcriptomes from 327 patients, with no new intervention cohort. Both Crohn candidate rows belong to this same analysis.

limitations.text: The analysis used one transcriptome dataset; the authors note potential selection bias and the need for experimental confirmation.
Candidate nomination cannot quantify patient benefit, and neither drug was tested as a Crohn treatment in this report.

effects.recordedResult: Ivermectin inhibited growth of WNT-TCF-dependent colorectal xenografts; TCF-independent growth was not similarly inhibited, and constitutively active TCF rescued growth. These experiments support a pathway hypothesis rather than clinical colorectal-cancer efficacy.

synthesisRows.title: NSCLC xenograft growth in mice
synthesisRows.use: Experimental fenbendazole cancer investigation
synthesisRows.population: A549 human NSCLC xenografts in female athymic mice, with supporting NSCLC cell experiments
synthesisRows.comparison: Fenbendazole versus untreated/control xenografts
synthesisRows.formulation: Fenbendazole 1 mg per mouse every second day

finding.text: Fenbendazole reduced A549 xenograft size and weight in the reported mouse experiment, with supporting apoptosis and vascularity assays. This does not establish cancer control or safe dosing in people.

synthesisRows.magnitudeText: Reduced xenograft size and weight in mice; no human efficacy estimate.
synthesisRows.evidenceBase: Cell and mouse xenograft experiments; no human randomized trial

limitations.text: Randomization, allocation concealment and blinded tumor assessment were not established; a numeric effect and confidence interval were not extracted.
This veterinary-drug experiment does not establish human NSCLC treatment, survival benefit, or safety. Separate human liver-injury reports remain safety evidence, not cancer-efficacy evidence.

pending: Additional corpus sources and independent scientific review remain pending.
